title: NA/EU/APAC GPU Fleet Velocity and Buffer Planner — Q2 2026 runbook
content:
Purpose:
This working runbook maps expected velocity (time-to-activate) for additional GPU capacity across North America, Europe, and APAC for Q2 2026, and defines a pragmatic buffer strategy (hot/warm/cold lanes) aligned to product demand patterns and vendor lead times. This is an operations-first document — lean, with assumptions, scenario tables, a sprint-level timeline, and clear action owners.

Summary of recommendations (top of doc):
- Target active fleet by 2026-06-30: NA = 1,150 A100-equivalent GPUs; EU = 650 H100-equivalent GPUs; APAC = 380 mixed L4/H100-equivalent GPUs. These totals are expressed as "A100-equivalent" for costing/throughput normalization.
- Buffer policy: hot pool = 8-12% of region active capacity; warm pool = 18-25%; cold reserve = contractual headroom (vendor + lead-time insurance) = 10%.
- Activation velocity expectations: typical spin-up time = 1.5–3 weeks (NA), 2–5 weeks (EU), 3–6 weeks (APAC) depending on instance family and network setup.
- Primary risk: delayed vendor delivery in APAC (estimated 3–4 week mean delay) and EU customs/networking window risk for on-prem partner installs.

Assumptions baked into numbers:
- Conversion factors used: 1 H100 ~= 1.9 A100-equivalent for throughput-sensitive workloads; L4 ~= 0.35 A100-equivalent for CPU-bound/light-fp workloads. Normalized numbers rounded to nearest 5.
- Average baseline utilization target (cost-optimized) = 50% across a rolling 7d window; short-term peak allowance up to 80% for 3 hours/day at regional primetime.
- Workloads mix: 55% low-latency chat/assistant, 25% batch embeddings, 20% reranking/evals. This drives differing scheduling and batch tolerance.
- Quantization mix targeted for Q2: 40% int8/4-bit quantized instances for batch, 60% full-precision for low-latency critical routes.

Velocity model (high level):
- Activation lead time = vendor provisioning + cloud zone configuration + VPC/network + autoscaling test windows.
- Typical path: order -> vendor confirmation (1–5d) -> infra provisioning (3–14d) -> network + KMS + test harness (3–7d) -> canary traffic (2–5d) -> full route flip.
- Parallelization: order region + zone lanes in parallel to reduce calendar time; two parallel vendors per region recommended to lower single-vendor risk.

Region-specific details:
- North America (NA):
  - Baseline need by EOW 2026-04-30: +300 A100-equivalent GPUs to support growth. End of Q2 target: 1,150 active.
  - Typical activation velocity: 10–21 days. Hot pool target = 90–140 GPUs. Warm pool = 200–280 GPUs. Cold reserve = contractual 120 GPUs.
  - Preferred instance families: A100 and H100 mix (for peak-retargeted routes). Use reserved H100s for sustained throughput lanes.
- Europe (EU):
  - Baseline need by EOW 2026-05-15: +220 H100-equivalent. End of Q2 target: 650 active.
  - Activation velocity: 14–35 days (customs, vendor handoff, network approvals inflate schedule). Hot pool target = 50–80 GPUs. Warm pool = 120–160 GPUs. Cold reserve = vendor buffer 65 GPUs.
  - Notes: prioritize placing warm pool in two different clouds to reduce inter-cloud network blast radius.
- APAC:
  - Baseline need by EOW 2026-06-01: +150 A100-equivalent (mix L4 for inference-heavy low-cost lanes). End of Q2 target: 380 active.
  - Activation velocity: 21–42 days (longest in the tri-region set). Hot pool target = 30–45 GPUs. Warm pool = 70–95 GPUs. Cold reserve = vendor contractual 40 GPUs.
  - Notes: local carrier/networking and occasional vendor prequalification are primary schedule blockers.

Scenario matrix (short text matrix):
- Conservative scenario (vendor delays): require 20% higher warm+cold buffer; push non-critical batch routes to cross-region fallback (NA -> EU) for short windows.
- Aggressive scenario (market demand spike): accelerate procurement and accept a 4–6 week burn on burst budget; enable autoscale-burst to managed spot lanes for up to 15% of capacity.
- Cost-optimized scenario: raise quantization to 60% for batch and embeddings; target baseline utilization 58–65% before committing new hardware.

Week-by-week rollout (Q2 sprint map):
- Week 1 (2026-04-01 to 04-07): procurement orders for NA + EU warm pools; finalize vendor SOWs; open INFRA-1123 to track NA orders.
- Week 2 (04-08 to 04-14): cloud infra provisioning in NA zones; network/KMS tickets started; quick smoke tests for staging.
- Week 3 (04-15 to 04-21): canary routing to new NA hot pool; verify KV cache behavior at scale; perf regression hip-checks.
- Week 4 (04-22 to 04-28): ramp NA to 60% of target; begin EU provisioning in parallel.
- Weeks 5–7 (04-29 to 05-19): EU activation window, APAC procurement queues submitted; run two-week soak for NA routes.
- Weeks 8–12 (05-20 to 06-30): APAC provisioning and final warm/cold validations; full end-of-quarter capacity verification and cost/latency baseline report.

Operational playbook (short):
- Canary/rollback policy: 5–10% of traffic to new capacity for 48–72h; automatic rollback trigger on +25% p50 latency or +3x error rate.
- Autoscale-burst: cap burst to 15% of region active pool and 10% of daily spend to limit surprises.
- Observability: add per-region token-level billing dashboards and p50/p95 latency breakouts by route.

Action items and owners (short list):
- Marcus Lee: finalize SOW with Vendor B for NA H100 tranche by 2026-02-20.
- Aisha Patel: open network/KMS runbook PR and attach to INFRA-1123 by 2026-02-16.
- Lina Gomez: coordinate EU customs paperwork and partner contacts; identify alternate cloud lane by 2026-02-22.
- Tom Harrington: schedule APAC partner kickoff and initial lead-time test; capture vendor delay metrics for Q2 retros by 2026-03-01.

Unresolved questions / tradeoffs to resolve in review: (notes-to-self style)
- Should we accept the higher cost of H100 reserved for EU to reduce latency, or use a cross-region warm pool and accept increased tail latencies?
- Is the 10% cold reserve sufficient given dual-vendor strategy? What is our risk tolerance if two vendors have correlated delays?
- For APAC, does it make sense to pre-stage container images + model caches in edge zones to shave off 3–5 days in activation?

Appendix (quick reference numbers):
- End-of-Q2 targets (A100-equivalent): NA 1150, EU 650, APAC 380.
- Target regional hot/warm/cold split (percent): hot 8–12%, warm 18–25%, cold 8–12% (plus contractual).
- Key tickets/refs: INFRA-1123 (NA orders), INFRA-1178 (EU customs), INFRA-1199 (APAC partner kickoff).

Notes on doc hygiene: this is a working draft intended for the infra + solutions-eng sync on 2026-02-19. Expect iteration after vendor responses and finance cost sign-off.

-- end of runbook draft --
